_comment: VR TUNING, per venue. Edit this file to change how VR feels; edit
components-v5/shared/data/scenes.json to change what the site IS.
THE SPLIT: scenes.json owns scene DATA — which GLB, which navmesh, which
POIs, which floor plan — and both the flat site and VR read it, so a model
swap or a new destination reaches both with no duplication. This file owns
everything that is a HEADSET question and has no flat equivalent, or whose
flat value is wrong in VR.
Every value here is optional. Anything omitted falls back to the flat
value from scenes.json, or to the defaults in ./index.ts, so a venue can
be added to scenes.json and work in VR before anyone tunes it.
ANGLES ARE DEGREES here, unlike scenes.json, which stores radians because
that is what its player feeds to a THREE.Euler. Degrees are what a person
editing a spawn actually wants to type, and the XR origin is set from
FIRST PERSON AND DOLL HOUSE ARE SEPARATE. They are two different views of
the same building with nothing in common: one puts you on the floor at
human scale, the other puts the whole venue on a table in front of you.
A single spawn cannot describe both.

defaults.//: Applied to any venue that does not override them.
//fov: PREVIEW ONLY. Inside an immersive session the headset supplies its own
projection and this is ignored entirely — it sets the flat canvas behind
the gate, which is what a desktop visitor sees. Kept per-venue because
that preview is the only picture some people will ever see of a venue.
//cameraHeight: NOT added to the XR origin. A headset reports the wearer's real standing
height, so adding an authored eye height on top puts their head through
the ceiling. It is recorded because it is the honest statement of how
tall a person is in this model's units, and a value far from ~1.7 means
the model is not authored in metres — which is worth knowing before
blaming the locomotion for feeling wrong.
//locomotion: moveSpeed is metres per second at full stick. Scale it to the venue, not
to taste: the same 1.4 that feels like a walk in a room feels like
wading across a stadium. turnSpeed (degrees/second) is a COMFORT limit
and should stay put. teleportSeconds is how long a 'travel to' glide
takes — long enough to read the journey, short enough not to be a wait.
//dollHouse: position: where the table sits, in metres from the XR origin, which is at
FLOOR level — so y is measured from the floor and wants to be near eye
height. Negative z is in front of you.
tableSpan: how wide the model reads on that table, in metres. The model
is scaled to fit its largest dimension into this, so one number covers
a hotel room and a stadium.
tilt: degrees about X. 90 is a straight plan view; 60 is a three-quarter
view that shows the venue has height.
spin: degrees about Y, for pointing a particular face at the viewer.
tiltRange: how far the thumbstick may tilt it, [min, max].

//hidden: NOT LISTED IN VR. It stays in scenes.json and the flat site still
shows it — this is a VR-only decision, which is what this file is for.
It is a single hotel room among three event venues: no POIs, no floor
plan, nothing to walk to and nothing to look up. In the flat site it
sits in a sidebar where an extra entry costs nothing; in a headset it
is a row in the Venues panel that reloads a model to show you a room.
hotel-room.//: A single room. Slow, or you cross it in two steps.
hotel-room.//dollHouse: A four-metre room on a 1.6 m table is nearly life-size; brought in closer and tipped nearer to plan so the layout reads.

memorial.//firstPerson: y is the authored concourse height. The navmesh spans 33 m of tiers, so its lowest point is NOT this floor — see the note in experience/session.
memorial.//: Concourses and stands — long, mostly straight runs.

stadium.//cameraHeight: Not authored flat either; the default stands.
stadium.//firstPerson: y is the Gate 1 concourse, 40 m above the pitch the navmesh bottoms out at.
stadium.//: The biggest by a wide margin: ~1 km corner to corner.
